blockers.title: The new volumeConstraint branches conflict with surviving unconditional install-root volume MUSTs
evidence: volumeConstraint and resolutionPredicate now say PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED has no object-path volume equality and EXTERNAL-ORIGIN does not require install-root volume equality.

filesystemMeasurementTarget.rule still says all relevant later resolutions MUST occupy the verifiedInstallRoot volume and that any object outside it refuses. sameVolume.retained still says step 3 compares both type and install-root volume without a tag condition.

loaderTraces.volumeEquality likewise remains unconditional: it refuses unless every later observed volume and filesystem token equal the preselection values. That directly rejects EXTERNAL-ORIGIN and cannot be satisfied by the PATHLESS inapplicable variant.

All of these clauses are normative and on the v13 roster. Nothing establishes precedence, so one implementation must refuse the new lawful branches while another may follow resolutionPredicate and allow them.
blockers.impact: PTCB-V12-B1 remains live: OS ABI can still be rejected by the surviving universal rule, and declared external system dependencies have contradictory allow/refuse outcomes. The contract cannot deterministically qualify its mandatory taxonomy.
blockers.requiredRepair: Replace filesystemMeasurementTarget.rule, sameVolume.retained, and volumeEquality with tag-dispatched rules. INSTALL-ROOT-VOLUME alone compares to the preselection volume/type; PATHLESS uses only its attestation join and forbids volume fields; EXTERNAL-ORIGIN uses its signed external-origin evidence and must not be sent through install-root equality.

shouldFix.title: The volumeConstraint event forms are not a closed, serialized tagged union
evidence: volumeConstraint calls itself a closed tagged union, but each tag is only a prose string; no exact tag-object serialization, allowed fields, or extras-rejected rule is defined for the signed entry.

laterEventVolumeFields says the PATHLESS variant emits no observed volume, while the same object still carries an unconditional required list containing observedVolumeIdentity and observedFilesystemTypeToken. No actual tagged inapplicable object shape is supplied.

pathlessObservation is a signed policy label, but retainedEventSchema has no observed pathlessObservation field or closed observation shape. evidenceJoin says later events join it without naming where the actual attestation observation is retained or how it equals the signed declaration.

macOS f_fsid, Linux decodedMountPoint/device, and linuxSelectedMountRecordIdentity still have no canonical retained serialization. volumeEquality continues to cite 'the closed form above', but no such form exists. EXTERNAL-ORIGIN requires later volume fields yet defines no equality or signed join for those observations.
shouldFix.impact: Producers can encode different signed tags and OS identities, a pathless refusal/allow event has no unique retained representation, and an external event carries observations that no verifier knows how to join. The branch policy therefore is not independently checkable from the retained evidence.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define exact signed tag objects and exhaustive per-tag event variants. Give PATHLESS a retained observed attestation field and exact join; give INSTALL-ROOT the serialized OS volume/type forms and preselection equality; give EXTERNAL an explicit observed-origin/volume form and join; reject all extra and cross-tag fields.

shouldFix.title: The admitted preselection event still requires base fields that do not exist before profile selection
evidence: filesystemMeasurementTarget is computed before platformProfile selection, yet retainedEventSchema lists completePlatformProfileKey on every event and does not mark it absent or deferred on eventKind=preselection.

The preselection variant also has no required/absent rules for taxonomyClass, taggedEvidenceForm, route, or companionObservation even though it is not a TCB-member resolution. Only resolvedObjectIdentity and allowlistMatch receive explicit preselection absence rules, while enforcedOutcome is assigned the unrelated value inapplicable.

Exactly-one cardinality and runIdentity now land, but the base-event conditional shape is still open; producers can either invent a not-yet-selected profile key and taxonomy event or omit apparently required fields.
shouldFix.impact: The one preselection record cannot be serialized deterministically at the time whose ordering is security-critical, and a reviewer cannot distinguish a retrospectively rewritten selection record from the required preselection observation.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Define an exhaustive preselection event variant: identify fields required at observation time, fields forbidden, and any fields appended only after selection with a separately retained binding/sequence rule. Prefer a run-level preselection record if completePlatformProfileKey is not available until the next step.

shouldFix.title: The Linux 'non-yielding sequence' is neither implementable nor the required before-and-after process check
evidence: observerProcess still requires {pid,starttime} immediately before and after mountinfo. The new namespace sequence enumerates only one {pid,starttime} read, then ns-before, mountinfo, and ns-after; its statement that any pair mismatch refuses has no second pair in that sequence to compare.

Multiple procfs reads are separate syscalls. A user-space verifier cannot guarantee that it will not sleep, fault, block, or be scheduler-preempted between them, so 'MUST NOT sleep' and 'one non-yielding sequence' are not a reproducible qualification property and have no retained proof.

If the observer reads another verifier process, making the observer non-yielding does not freeze that target against an A-to-B-to-A namespace transition. Adding the selected mount record improves retarget detection but is not an atomic process/namespace snapshot.
shouldFix.impact: One implementation must fail every run because it cannot prove non-yielding execution, while another may ignore the MUST and retain a baseline assembled across different process/namespace states. The v12 ABA advisory is not closed by this sequence.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Specify an implementable stable-observation protocol: include process identity both before and after the namespace/mountinfo reads, use a dedicated immutable verifier or freeze/coordinate the target, hold stable namespace/process handles where available, and retain the exact sequence evidence. Do not make scheduler non-preemption a conformance condition.

advisories.title: The old conflated verifiedInstallRoot equality remains beside the new split equality
advisories.evidence: tcbCarrier.verifiedInstallRoot correctly separates signedTokenBytes from hostLocalCanonicalPath, but signedBinding.serialization.equality still says one UTF-8 byte comparison occurs after NFC and after canonicalization. The two clauses define different domains without precedence.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The new carrier clause states the intended two-domain rule clearly, and the join/canonicalization clauses remain fail-closed; this is a stale duplicate rather than a missing operation.
advisories.suggestedRepair: Replace the stale serialization equality with a pointer to tcbCarrier.verifiedInstallRoot.equality or restate only signedTokenBytes there.

advisories.title: PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED lacks an explicit only-if class restriction
advisories.evidence: pathlessClasses says its members MUST use the PATHLESS tag, but no reciprocal rule says the tag is forbidden for every class outside that closed member set. A file-backed class that also permits PLATFORM-ATTESTED evidence can therefore be read as eligible to select the pathless branch and skip origin/path checks.
advisories.whyOnlyAdvisory: The tag prose says it is for a class with no required object path and currently names OS ABI, so the intended restriction is evident even though the closed compatibility rule is one-way.
advisories.suggestedRepair: State PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED is lawful if and only if class is a member of the closed pathlessClasses set; all other classes refuse that tag.
